coaching.text: ShotKam describes diminishing/collapsing lead immediately before trigger as associated with eyes moving to the barrel, gun movement slowing/stopping and a common miss behind.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: ShotKam Station 4 guidance warns that consciously measuring lead with the eyes slows gun movement and produces diminishing lead; it advises concentrating on the clay rather than the lead.
coaching.label: DIRECT

coaching.text: ShotKam youth-coaching material describes collapsing lead when a shooter becomes barrel aware and discusses proprioceptive awareness as part of learning the movement.
coaching.label: DIRECT

diagnose.symptom: lead opens then contracts immediately before trigger, often with gun-speed loss
candidate_mechanisms: indecision / low trust in committed pull-away
diagnose.question: Does the forward relationship develop normally and then collapse as gun angular speed falls? If gaze evidence exists, does attention leave the clay during the same interval?
diagnose.interpretation: Combined separation collapse plus gun deceleration raises the probability of barrel checking. Without direct gaze evidence, keep the diagnosis probabilistic and retain alternative causes.
diagnose.fix: Keep visual attention on the clay and trust the committed move; compare against a deliberate measuring/barrel-checking condition without prescribing a numerical lead.
diagnose.retest: Same hidden presentation family first, then vary speed/distance while preserving method and target-focus instruction.

holds: Do not encode barrel checking as a guaranteed behind miss.
Do not claim ShotKam coaching material alone proves the complete neurological or proprioceptive mechanism.
Do not give Ellis exact lead, miss vector, range or oracle correction through this diagnostic.
